articles.title: Two women from South Australia activated a satellite emergency device after encountering difficult conditions on Tasmania's Western Arthur Range: A rescue team had to walk in as helicopter could not reach
articles.summary: The wilderness holds secrets of nature that remain unexplored.
articles.body: The wilderness holds secrets of nature that remain unexplored. In the modern world, it also offers an offline world away from notifications, traffic, and the city bustle. It is an occasional opportunity to wake up to the sound of the birds and the wind through the trees, making a trip to the wilderness all the more exciting. However, we humans are also trained to live in civilised settings. This can make unpredictable situations like bad weather or wildlife encounters difficult for adventurers to handle.Two women from South Australia recently discovered this while exploring Tasmania's spectacular Western Arthur Range, where difficult conditions forced them to call for help. It became a story of a carefully executed rescue operation possible because of an emergency satellite device, a helicopter and a search-and-rescue team that had to hike through the rugged landscape because the aircraft could not reach them directly.When a wilderness adventure takes an unexpected turnThe two bushwalkers, aged 58 and 26, were exploring Tasmania's beautiful remote south-western wilderness when conditions became difficult enough for them to seek assistance. The women were appropriately equipped for their overnight camping trip, along with the required communication equipment. However, they faced unpredictable weather conditions, which led them to ask for immediate help.At around 8 pm on Saturday, November 14, 2026, the duo activated their personal locator beacon (PLB) from a walking track near Haven Lake, reporting that they needed help due to the conditions. Their distress signal alerted emergency services, setting a rescue operation into motion.A helicopter rescue that turned into a walking missionWeather conditions prevented Tasmania Police from operating the rescue helicopter to reach the women directly. Instead, at approximately 5 am on Sunday, November 15, the helicopter dropped a search-and-rescue crew at Arthurs Plains. From there, the rescuers had to continue on foot through the challenging terrain to reach the stranded bushwalkers.The team eventually located the women at around 8 am, roughly three hours after being dropped off. The duo underwent a medical check-up as a precaution and, fortunately, neither required medical treatment. They were subsequently transported towards Hobart.The Tasmania Police rescue announcement confirmed that the women's personal locator beacon helped ensure a quick emergency response.The little emergency device that can make a big differenceThe personal locator beacon (PLB) was the device that proved extremely helpful for the two women stranded in the remote wilderness of Tasmania. Unlike an ordinary mobile phone, a satellite emergency beacon is designed to send a distress signal from remote locations where conventional mobile networks may not be available. When activated, a compatible 406 MHz distress beacon transmits an emergency signal that the international COSPAS-SARSAT satellite system can detect. The alert is then relayed to the relevant rescue coordination authorities, who can organise assistance.The Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) explains how emergency beacons work and why registering them is important. It highlights that rescue operations can look different, as rescue times depend on factors such as weather, terrain, distance and accessibility. In this particular incident, the beacon helped emergency services respond quickly, even though the helicopter was unable to reach the women directly.A reminder for everyone heading into the wildTasmania Police used the incident to remind bushwalkers about the importance of carrying adequate food, water, warm clothing, emergency shelter and reliable communication equipment. Hikers are also advised to share their intended route and expected return time with someone before setting out.Another useful precaution is to pack clothing and essential equipment separately in waterproof bags so that everything remains dry if the weather changes.And perhaps the most important advice is not to wait until a situation becomes dangerous before asking for help. If conditions deteriorate, contacting emergency services early is often the wisest decision.Though in this situation, the two women were fortunate to return without injuries. Their experience offers a lesson for future adventurers to carry proper communication equipment that can be utilised to access help in emergency situations. While adventure is all about exploring the unknown, one should never go unprepared, considering their own safety.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Pretty foolish’: Musk admits $500m gamble on Trump failed in midterms, wishes he could ‘rewind’ the clock
articles.summary: Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has said he feels 'pretty foolish' about spending nearly $500 million backing Republican candidates in the US midterm
articles.body: Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has said he feels 'pretty foolish' about spending nearly $500 million backing Republican candidates in the US midterm elections, admitting that his political spending failed to deliver the results he had hoped for after Democrats secured victories in key races.Speaking via videolink at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the Tesla and SpaceX chief executive said he would have spent less had he known how the elections would turn out.“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said.Reflecting on his political objective, Musk said he had wanted either the presidency, the House of Representatives or the Senate to be controlled by the opposing party.“That was my actual goal here, which failed by the way,” he said.Musk also distanced himself from the Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, despite previously describing himself as MAGA and even “dark gothic MAGA”.“I’m not MAGA,” he said, according to The New York Times. “If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”“There are positives and negatives in both parties,” he added, seeking to present himself as less closely aligned with either political camp.The remarks marked Musk's most detailed assessment of his political spending following the Republican setbacks. According to The New York Times, his contributions represented the largest amount spent by a non-candidate in a single US election cycle.Among the candidates he backed was Texas Senate contender Ken Paxton, who reportedly received around $220 million in support from Musk. Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico.Musk acknowledged that the election results had challenged the assumption that large financial contributions could determine political outcomes.“It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money,” he said.“Obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here,” he added.He also said, “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”Musk had previously spent more than $250 million supporting US President Donald Trump's return to the White House and briefly led the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) before a public fallout with the president. The two have since reconciled, and Musk continued to support Republican candidates backed by Trump.Beyond electoral politics, Musk discussed his business interests, including the possibility of merging SpaceX and Tesla. He also defended his position on Ukraine's use of Starlink, saying, “Do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Cambridge growers donate leftover pumpkins for free meal kits
articles.summary: "It's a really tough time for a lot of people," a sustainable food organisation says.
articles.body:
Leftover pumpkins have helped a sustainable food organisation provide its 1,000th free meal to low-income households.

Cambridge Sustainable Food started producing recipe kits earlier this year using fruit and vegetables that would have otherwise gone to waste.

The group received masses of pumpkins from local farmers after Halloween, including about 300kg (661lb) of them from one supplier alone.

Alex Vardill, from the organisation, said many of the meal kits had been received by families who sometimes struggled to access fresh produce.

"This has been a real help with improving that access at a time when food is really expensive," the 25-year-old said.

"They provide everything you need to make a meal in one bag, already measured out, with a recipe there in front of you."

The kits are funded by Cambridge City Council and South Cambridgeshire District Council.

They are distributed by food hubs – a mini-supermarket where anyone can go to access low-cost food – and other local organisations.

The Halloween leftovers were used in 50 pumpkin and lentil soup recipe kits, which were assembled by a team of volunteers this week.

The organisation is based in a warehouse in the Barnwell area of Cambridge, which is stocked with food donated by local supermarkets and residents.

Vardill, who also volunteers at a community kitchen, said they had noticed an increased demand for both services.

"It's a really tough time for a lot of people," they added.

The recipe kit initiative launched in July, making use of excess blackberries.

Since then, other recipes have been themed around leftover tomatoes, courgettes, and apples.

articles.title: The Xi-Putin-Trump summit will not be a ‘new Yalta’
articles.summary: The three leaders have divergent geopolitical goals and visions for the world order.
articles.body:
On November 19, the leaders of China, the United States and Russia will gather for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of an annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The three have never met for formal trilateral talks, and some commentators are already calling the meeting “historic”.

In Moscow, many observers see the gathering as a “new Yalta” – another conference to divide the world into spheres of influence, similar to the one held in 1945 between Britain, the USSR and the US.

This thinking reflects Russian President Vladimir Putin’s own worldview. It is perhaps unsurprising that he was the one to propose the trilateral meeting during a call with US President Donald Trump in October.

A “new Yalta”, however, appears to be more of a case of wishful thinking than a realistic possibility. In 1945, the Soviet Union, the US and Britain came together after emerging victorious from the second world war, in which they fought against a common enemy. Today, not only do they find themselves on opposing sides of various conflicts and disputes, but they also seem to disagree on how the world should run.

While all three powers speak of a new, multipolar world and formally reject the language of hegemony, they seem to have divergent understandings of what that means.

Moscow, for example, seeks to establish itself as one of the poles in a multipolar world and a regional leader in Eurasia.

Washington, on the other hand, wants to secure its status as the pre-eminent power, while Beijing remains preoccupied with pulling the Global South away from US leadership.

Therefore, the US and China are championing a bipolar system – a world shaped by the “G2” as Trump calls it – which Russia might be unhappy with but has no means of stopping.

This disparity of aspirations is also apparent at the economic level. While Russia has chosen a path towards archaisation and opposes almost any manifestations of progress, the US and China are leading the world in technological innovation and competing in spheres such as semiconductor production, mobile communications, space exploration, robotics, biotechnology and, most recently, artificial intelligence (AI). In all these spheres, Russia has fallen behind not years, but decades.

These divergent visions are reflected in the apparent disagreement over what this summit should be about.

Trump has said he would prefer to address nuclear disarmament, a topic that is unpopular in China given that it has the smallest nuclear arsenal of the three countries. Russia, too, is not very eager given that it is relying on its nuclear arsenal as the last remaining element of its great-power status.

Putin, on the other hand, wanted to focus the summit on the settlement of the Ukraine war without the Ukrainians and Europeans present. Yet, it is unclear what can be achieved in a sit-down with Trump and Xi Jinping, given Putin’s maximalist demands.

As the recent consultations in Abu Dhabi and Moscow demonstrated, the Russian president wants profound changes to the current European order that simply cannot be secured because they would be in violation of international law.

Even if a rollback of NATO might appeal to China, Putin’s insistence on violating the principle of sovereignty would be too much for Beijing. Therefore, I cannot imagine President Xi willingly engaging in discussions that are bound to face a dead end.

Instead of entertaining his guests’ unrealistic agendas, Xi is likely to yield to no more than a general declaration on cooperation and common understanding.

For him, the summit is a long-awaited – and much-deserved – foreign policy triumph, and an acknowledgement of China’s standing in the world.

After all, he will be hosting the leaders of the two states that Beijing had looked up to as superpowers for the better part of the last century. From the late 1940s, China was highly dependent on the USSR, and even after the Mao-Khrushchev break, it replicated many Soviet policies and technologies.

Then with the launch of market reforms in the late 1970s, Beijing gradually became the most talented disciple of the US-led West, masterfully convincing the Americans that its economic rise would benefit everyone while capturing global markets through formal acknowledgement of World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and intellectual property laws.

In this sense, it is highly symbolic that China welcomes the leaders of Russia and the US at a time when it dominates global manufacturing and trade, has the fastest-growing economy of the three powers, and is a frontrunner in the global technology race.

There is also quite the contrast between the level-headed Xi and his US and Russian counterparts, whose irresponsible policies have dragged their countries into disastrous wars they cannot win or get out of.

In the end, the summit may lay the foundations of a new trilateral format between China, the US and Russia. Each leader may have their own reasons to maintain it: Trump would like to continue with his unilateral policies, sidelining traditional allies; Putin desperately wants to become a part of something reminiscent of the old times when Moscow was a superpower; and Xi might use this format to institutionalise a G2+1, knowing that the +1 – Russia – will be dropped after the Ukraine war ends and the world’s attention to the Kremlin diminishes.

Yet, little of substance would come out of these meetings. These would not be venues where the pressing issues of the world would be resolved.

And in any case, Xi, Trump and Putin may not be capable of resolving them. After all, they belong to an outgoing generation of policymakers representing a world captured not so much by powerful ideologies or leadership aspirations, but rather by memories, nostalgia, old phobias and prejudices.

In the coming years, it may happen – as it did after the “old Yalta” – that they no longer occupy positions of power and a new generation will take their place, leading the world into a better future.

articles.title: Developer accused of 'vandalism' over loss of Kidlington trees
articles.summary: Bellway says the work has been done with an ecologist on site and in compliance with planning consent.
articles.body:
Work to gain access to land for a housing development and a new "super cycleway" has resulted in "environmental vandalism", councillors have said.

Kidlington Green councillors Ian Middleton and Fiona Mawson said residents were concerned by the number of hedgerows and trees recently cut down on Oxford Road.

Adjacent fields have planning permission for 800 homes as part of wider plans for more than 4,400 to be built in the area.

A spokesperson for developer Bellway said all the work had been done with an ecologist on site and complied with outline planning consent.

The cycleway would help connecting Kidlington to Oxford, running alongside the A4165, Oxford Road.

The route is expected to get busier with significant growth planned for north Oxford, including a potential new stadium for Oxford United.

According to Bellway, the trees and hedges were cut down between 26 October and 6 November to "create access" to the site planned for housing, as well as to "facilitate" the work for the cycleway.

The proposals include "significant landscaping and ecological enhancements" as well as 50% affordable housing and "other infrastructure", it said.

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

Middleton, the lead member for housing and greener communities at Cherwell District Council, said outline planning permission did not give the developer "unrestricted permission to carry out works".

He also said its actions were "nonsensical" and premature, given the cycle path was not "imminent".

"If all they needed was access, why have they ripped out an entire hedgerow?" he said.

"We knew some of this was going to be taken out, but it's the scale of it that's really impacted people and sent shock waves across the local community."

A spokesperson for Bellway said hit had been working with Cherwell District Council "to agree details of a replacement wildlife corridor," including planting 150 new trees.

articles.title: Guernsey's Storm Goretti response gets national attention
articles.summary: Two people involved in the clear-up visit Sheffield for a national tree expert forum.
articles.body:
Two members of an island's response to Storm Goretti have told of their "fascinating" experience taking questions from a national audience of tree experts.

Andy McCutcheon, the principal environment services officer at the States of Guernsey, and Hugo Ciotti, an arboricultural consultant, took part in the National Tree Officers' Conference, in Sheffield, England, earlier in November.

The pair's presentation walked through Guernsey's storm damage response and what it was like on the front line, clearing roads to help people.

Ciotti said there was "no shortage of interest" from the 200 attendees, who he said saw Guernsey as "a test bed in responding to storms" due to its geography.

The island was hit by severe wind speeds of 95mph (154km/h) on the night of 8 January, with thousands of trees lost and damage to properties .

About 100 roads across the island were closed due to fallen trees and debris.

Ciotti said: "The day was fascinating, with some excellent speakers and plenty of opportunities for sharing knowledge and best practice.

"Guernsey may be small, but I think they picked up on the fact that its position on the edge of the Atlantic makes it something of a test bed in responding to storms,.

"Everyone in the industry is mindful of the effects of our changing climate, so there was no shortage of interest."

McCutcheon said he was "delighted" Guernsey could make "an important contribution" to the forum.

He said: "The key learning we took to Sheffield was that storm response planning requires multi-agency coordination and resilience frameworks.

"As a small jurisdiction, the lessons we've learned over the past three years in responding to storms Ciarán and Goretti have given us a level of experience and insight that's worth sharing at a national level."

articles.title: Bodies of construction workers killed in New York building collapse being returned to Ecuador
articles.summary: The remains of one of two Ecuadorian construction workers killed when a building collapsed into an adjacent pit that was being excavated in New York were returned Wednesday to his home in Quisapincha, high in the country’s central Andean region.
articles.body: QUITO, Ecuador — The remains of one of two Ecuadorian construction workers killed when a building collapsed into an adjacent pit that was being excavated in New York were returned Wednesday to his home in Quisapincha, high in the country’s central Andean region. Relatives received the body of José Caguana, 26, in the rural town’s Bahía neighborhood, where his friends and family cried together as mournful Andean melodies played from a speaker. “So this is how it ends — to leave in search of a better life and come back as a corpse,” one of relatives, Segundo Caguana, told Quisapincha TV, his voice breaking with emotion. Gabriel Sigüenza, 22, also died in the collapse in Brooklyn, and his remains were expected to arrive Wednesday night in the port city of Guayaquil before being returned to his family in Cañar, in Ecuador’s southern Andes region. The Ecuadorian government paid for the repatriations, a foreign ministry statement said. Tens of thousands of Ecuadorians have migrated to the United States without authorization in recent years, seeking work as their country struggles with recurring economic and employment crises and rising violence. New York authorities said the collapse of the three-story building next to an excavation site killed eight people, including some from Ecuador, Mexico, Guatemala and Trinidad. The collapse remains under investigation. City officials said authorities had determined that the demolition of the previous building lacked adequate safeguards, and court records show the construction company faced two lawsuits accusing it of damaging adjacent buildings in other projects. The building that collapsed also had a record of safety violations.

articles.title: Senegal boat disaster: Dozens missing as boat with 100 migrants sinks
articles.summary: Some local media report that at least four bodies have been recovered.
articles.body:
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat reportedly carrying about 100 migrants capsized off the coast.

Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported that at least four bodies have been recovered. Dozens of people are still missing.

Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.

This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.

Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).

"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.

A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, AFP reported.

Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.

At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about a renewed increase in irregular departure by migrants hoping to reach Europe.

He instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving the dangerous journeys and proposing measures to tackle the problem.

Following last month's tragedy, Faye had urged Senegalese people not to risk their lives attempting the dangerous sea crossings.

Many thousands of people from West Africa have died or gone missing trying to flee conflict, authoritarian rule or poverty in recent years.

The UN's migration agency IOM said last month that it had recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year alone.

It warned the figures were likely to be an underestimate, as many boats disappear without leaving survivors or a trace.

As it has become more difficult to reach Europe through North Africa, due to tighter controls and increased co-operation with European countries, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands.

They often travel in wooden boats known as pirogues that are frequently overloaded and not suited to such long voyages across the Atlantic Ocean.

Most migrants arriving in the Canary Islands this year are from Senegal, according to the UN.

They are driven to leave home by limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks, according to the IOM.

On 7 November, El Hierro, one of the Canary Islands, declared a state of emergency following a surge in migrant arrivals.

It said more than 3,300 people had reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of the month. This amounts to almost a third of the island's population.

articles.title: Delhi-Mumbai bullet train: The missing link between India’s major economy
articles.summary: Imagine covering nearly 1,400km between Delhi and Mumbai in under six hours, instead of the 15 hours 40 minutes taken by the fastest regular train
articles.body: Imagine covering nearly 1,400km between Delhi and Mumbai in under six hours, instead of the 15 hours 40 minutes taken by the fastest regular train currently connecting the two cities.The prospect remains a long-term possibility, not an announced travel-time target. But it points to a larger question about India's bullet train ambitions: If high-speed rail is intended to connect major economic centres, why does the proposed Delhi-Ahmedabad corridor — a potential extension of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train line towards the national capital — remain outside the list of new corridors?The proposed Delhi-Ahmedabad corridor and the under-construction Mumbai-Ahmedabad line could eventually form parts of a larger high-speed rail network.The first would connect Delhi and the National Capital Region with Rajasthan and Gujarat, while the second is being built to link Ahmedabad with Mumbai, India's financial capital.Together, they could create a high-speed passenger corridor connecting some of western and northern India's largest urban and commercial centres. But that would require the Delhi-Ahmedabad project to move beyond planning, along with further decisions on network integration and a direct Delhi-Mumbai service.For now, the contrast is stark. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is under construction, while Delhi-Ahmedabad has yet to become a sanctioned project under execution.Delhi-Ahmedabad: The missing linkThe proposed Delhi-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor is envisaged as an approximately 886km route, with a journey time of less than four hours. The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) has drawn up the detailed project report, and 15 stations have been proposed across Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Gujarat. However, the corridor remains in the planning stage and is likely to take shape only in the latter half of the decade.Manesar and Rewari are the two proposed stations in Haryana. The route will originate at Dwarka Sector 21 in Delhi and enter Gurgaon at Chauma. It will run along the Dwarka Expressway up to Ramprastha City in Sector 37D before turning towards the Delhi-Jaipur railway line. The alignment will cross the KMP Expressway before joining the Delhi-Jaipur highway at Shahjahanpur toll plaza, near the Haryana-Rajasthan border.The 15 proposed stations are Dwarka in Delhi; IMT Manesar and Rewari in Haryana; Behror, Shahpura, Jaipur, Ajmer, Vijaynagar, Bhilwara, Chittorgarh, Udaipur and Dungarpur in Rajasthan; and Himmatnagar, Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad in Gujarat.The entire corridor is proposed to be elevated. At present, a train journey between Delhi and Ahmedabad takes around 14 hours. The proposed bullet train could reduce this to less than four hours.Explaining the choice of alignment, an NHSRCL official told TOI, "We have chosen this alignment (along the rail line and highway) to ensure that land acquisition is minimal. In such mega projects, maximum time gets spent in acquiring privately owned land. While the alignment is final, acquiring land is yet to begin."The official said the preparatory work would itself take considerable time before construction could begin.The corridor was among the early routes considered in India's bullet train plans, after Mumbai-Ahmedabad. However, the two projects are at very different stages. Mumbai-Ahmedabad has moved into construction, while Delhi-Ahmedabad has not received the same implementation push.The omission is significant because Delhi-Ahmedabad could serve a wider purpose than simply reducing travel time between two cities. It could become the missing northern link in a broader high-speed passenger connection between Delhi, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Mumbai.That does not mean the route has been formally abandoned or that its revival has been ruled out. But without project sanction, a firm implementation plan and construction, the corridor remains an ambition rather than an imminent transport alternative.Why connecting the economic centres mattersThe economic case for high-speed rail is not limited to faster journeys. Reliable, frequent connections between major cities can make it easier for businesses to operate across regions, improve access to jobs and education, and enable people to travel between commercial centres without spending most of a day in transit.Delhi and the National Capital Region are major centres of government, services, trade and corporate activity. Ahmedabad and Gujarat form part of a significant industrial and commercial belt, while Mumbai remains a major financial centre and gateway for domestic and international business.A connected Delhi-Ahmedabad-Mumbai high-speed rail network could bring these economic regions closer in practical terms. It could make same-day business travel easier, improve access to skilled workers and strengthen links between companies, suppliers and service providers.The benefits would depend on more than speed alone. Station locations, service frequency, ticket prices, local transport connections and the time required to reach stations would all influence whether passengers and businesses actually use the network.The corridor could also improve connectivity for cities between the largest metropolitan centres. If stations are well integrated with local transport and economic hubs, places along the route could gain better access to larger markets and employment centres.However, these are potential benefits, not guaranteed outcomes. They would depend on the final alignment, the services offered and the wider development of the cities connected by the line.A passenger network with a wider economic purposeThe comparison with India's freight corridors helps explain the larger infrastructure argument.The Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors were developed to improve the movement of goods, increase freight capacity and reduce pressure on heavily used conventional railway routes. The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor links the Delhi-NCR region with the Jawaharlal Nehru Port area near Mumbai, strengthening the movement of cargo between industrial and consumption centres and a major port.A Delhi-Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train connection would serve a different purpose. Freight corridors move goods; high-speed rail is designed primarily for passengers. But both reflect the importance of dedicated infrastructure that connects economic centres more efficiently.The road network offers another comparison. The Golden Quadrilateral connected Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata through a major highway network, improving road links between some of India's largest urban and commercial centres.A high-speed rail network would not replace highways or freight routes, but will add another layer of connectivity for passenger movement.The underlying principle is similar: transport infrastructure can support economic integration when it reduces the time, cost and uncertainty involved in moving people or goods between regions.For bullet trains, the challenge is to ensure that major corridors connect into a coherent network rather than remain isolated projects. A Delhi-Ahmedabad line linked operationally with Mumbai-Ahmedabad could be an important step in that direction, provided the government decides to pursue such an extension.Mumbai-Ahmedabad is moving; Delhi-Ahmedabad is notThe 508km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is India's first dedicated bullet train project. It is being developed with Japanese technical and financial assistance and is planned to have 12 stations across Maharashtra, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Gujarat.The line is designed for speeds of up to 350kmph, with an operational speed of 320kmph. The fastest services are expected to cover the route in around two hours. In July 2026, the government said the first service was expected to begin in August 2027 on the Surat-Vapi section. The full corridor is a separate, longer-term undertaking.The project has faced delays, including challenges over land acquisition in Maharashtra, and its costs have risen substantially from the original estimate. Nevertheless, construction is under way, making it the country's only sanctioned high-speed rail project under execution.Delhi-Ahmedabad has not reached that stage. Even if a detailed proposal exists, moving from planning to implementation would require decisions on the project report, financing, alignment, land acquisition, clearances and construction.This is why the two routes cannot yet be treated as one continuous bullet train service. A future Delhi-Mumbai connection would require more than the completion of the existing Mumbai-Ahmedabad line: the Delhi-Ahmedabad project would have to be taken forward, and a through-service and its operating arrangements would need to be established.Could the Gujarat election put the corridor back in focus?The next Gujarat Legislative Assembly election is scheduled for December 2027. The Delhi-Ahmedabad corridor could become a subject of renewed political and infrastructure debate in the run-up to the election, particularly because Gujarat is central to both the proposed Delhi-Ahmedabad link and the under-construction Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project.A project connecting Ahmedabad with Delhi could be presented as a further expansion of Gujarat's links with major economic centres. It could also fit into a broader pitch around investment, industrial development and connectivity.The more immediate question is whether the Centre will move the corridor forward through the required project and financing decisions.Seven new corridors — but Delhi-Ahmedabad is missingBudget 2026-27 announced seven new high-speed rail corridors as “growth connectors”, aimed at improving regional connectivity, supporting tourism and investment, and encouraging a shift from road and air travel to rail. Delhi-Varanasi was included, but Delhi-Ahmedabad was not.The announcement points to a broader ambition to connect major urban and economic centres through high-speed rail. Yet it also raises questions about sequencing: which corridors should be prioritised, how they would connect with one another, and how the government intends to finance a capital-intensive network.The Railway Ministry has cautioned that sanctioning a high-speed rail project depends on the outcome of detailed project reports, technical and economic feasibility and the availability of resources. Therefore, the seven announced corridors should not automatically be treated as projects that are ready for construction.Delhi-Ahmedabad's absence does not prove that it has been permanently shelved.But it does mean the corridor currently lacks the same political and administrative momentum as the newly announced proposals and the Mumbai-Ahmedabad line under construction.If the objective is to build a network that connects major economies, the question is not only how many corridors are announced, but how they fit together and which missing links are necessary to make the wider network useful.The missing link is about more than speedA Delhi-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor could eventually connect the national capital with Rajasthan and Gujarat, while the Mumbai-Ahmedabad line would bring Ahmedabad closer to Mumbai.If both are developed and integrated into a wider network, they could form the basis of a faster passenger connection between Delhi and Mumbai.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: All about the ‘Panchayat’ series ahead of season 5 release: From past seasons, when and where to watch, all about season 5, the full cast and plot, and more
articles.summary: Discover all the essential details about Panchayat season 5, including the release date, cast updates, plot twists, and previous seasons' highlights.
articles.body: ‘Panchayat’ premiered in 2020, and for the past six years it has been one of the most popular and highly watched OTT series. With multiple award wins and critical acclaim, it is also one of the highest-rated series as well and is soon going to be making a comeback with its fifth season. Here is all you need to know about the upcoming season and about the entire series.Premise of ‘Panchayat’First premiered on April 3, 2020, ‘Panchayat’ tells the story of Abhishek Tripathi (played by Jitendra Kumar), an engineering graduate who reluctantly takes a low-paying job as the secretary of a gram panchayat in the remote fictional Uttar Pradesh village of Phulera. What begins as a temporary stop while he preps for his CAT/MBA exams evolves into deep emotional entanglement with Phulera’s residents and petty rivalries, along with family drama.What happened at the end of season 4, and what to expect from season 5 of 'Panchayat'?Season 4 ended with a major political turnover after Pradhan Manju Devi (played by Neena Gupta) and her husband, Brij Bhushan Dubey (played by Raghubir Yadav), lost out on the village panchayat election to Kranti Devi (played by Sunita Rajwar) and her scheming husband, Bhushan Sharma, aka "Banrakas" (played by Durgesh Kumar), by 73 votes. The ending scenes then show Kranti Devi’s name replacing Manju Devi’s outside of the Panchayat office, shifting all the authority in Phulera to Bhushan’s camp.Another turn of events comes when Abhishek's CAT exam scores are revealed, and he finds out that he got 97 percent on it. However, instead of leaving right away, he chooses to stay in Phulera for a few more months.Season five is going to bring a lot of changes in Phulera, starting with new and fresh rivalries after Kranti Devi wins the election, along with shifting loyalties and whether all of this is nothing more than a publicity stunt. Not only that but going forward the show will also focus on Abhishek’s challenges as he faces a far more hostile and complicated workplace under the new leadership. Along with this, he has to juggle with the decision of what to do next after his CAT score and his pending MBA plans, all the while handling unresolved village responsibilities.When and where to watch ‘Panchayat’ season 5?The upcoming season of ‘Panchayat’ will be released on December 3, 2026, and will be available for streaming on Prime Video. All of the previous seasons of the beloved OTT series are also available for streaming on the same platform in case you wish to catch up on what has happened on the show so far.Cast members of ‘Panchayat’ season 5Many of the beloved cast members from the previous seasons are returning again. This includes Jitendra Kumar as Abhishek Tripathi, Neena Gupta as Manju Devi, Raghubir Yadav as Brij Bhushan Dubey, Sunita Rajwar as Kranti Devi, Durgesh Kumar as Bhushan Sharma, Faisal Malik as Prahladchand "Prahlad" Pandey, Chandan Roy as Vikas Shukla, Sanvikaa as Rinki, Ashok Pathak as Binod, and Pankaj Jha & Bulloo Kumar as Chandrakishore Singh & Madhav.What awards has ‘Panchayat’ won so far?Ever since its release, ‘Panchayat’ has won around 85 awards. This includes the award for Best Web Series (OTT) for Season 2 (2023) at IFFI (International Film Festival of India), Best Web Series (Comedy), and acting awards for cast members like Raghubir Yadav, Neena Gupta, and Sanvikaa at the Indian Television Academy (ITA) Awards, and many other awards from DPIFF, the Iconic Gold Awards, and the e4m Play Streaming Media Awards, and more.

articles.title: An Etihad Airways passenger was left without essential medicines and clothes during an 8-day pilgrimage tour after his luggage went missing; consumer commission has now ordered Rs 30,000 payout
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Etihad Airways to pay Rs 25,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs to a passenger
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Etihad Airways to pay Rs 25,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs to a passenger whose checked-in luggage went missing during an eight-day international pilgrimage tour. It held that the airline was deficient in service for failing to ensure timely delivery of his baggage, though the passenger had also contributed to his predicament by packing cash and essential medicines in it.Case backgroundAs per the commission order, Alfred Varghese was part of an eight-day group pilgrimage tour booked with Etihad Airways. The journey began from Thiruvananthapuram on December 20, 2015, and was scheduled to end on December 28. The tour covered Abu Dhabi, Jordan, Israel, Palestine and Egypt, for which he paid Rs 85,000.When Varghese arrived at Queen Alia Airport in Amman, Jordan, he found that his checked-in luggage had not arrived. The bag contained his clothes, cash, toiletries and essential medicines. He immediately reported the missing baggage to the airline's airport office.Varghese alleged that he suffered mental agony and hardship as he had no clothes to change, money to make purchases or medicines for his heart-related disorder. He said he had been taking regular medicines since 2007 and travelling without them posed a risk to his health.He further alleged that he requested the airline to arrange his return to India if the baggage could not be traced before his next flight, but the request was refused.The airline later traced the baggage, but it was sent to Thiruvananthapuram after Varghese had left Jordan. He alleged that despite repeated communications, the airline did not arrange to deliver it at any of the destinations during the remaining tour. The airline apologised and offered $40 through an email dated March 31, 2016. Varghese approached the commission alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice and sought Rs 2 lakh compensation.In its written statement, the airline admitted that his checked-in baggage was short-landed at Amman airport but denied that it contained essential medicines. It argued that its conditions of carriage prohibited passengers from keeping cash and essential medicines in checked-in baggage.The airline also said Varghese should have approached the tour operator for arrangements to return to India. It claimed the baggage was made available at Amman the next day, but he had already left for another destination. It further said he had not submitted bills for emergency purchases of clothes and toiletries despite being asked to do so for reimbursement.Commission's findingsThe bench of president P V Jayarajan and members Preetha G Nair and Viju V R held that the airline was deficient in service for failing to ensure timely delivery of the baggage. However, it also found that Varghese had contributed to his predicament by packing cash and essential medicines in checked-in luggage.The commission said an airline accepting checked-in baggage is duty-bound to ensure its safe and timely delivery."Once an airline accepts checked-in baggage from a passenger, it is duty-bound to ensure the safe and timely delivery of the same at the destination. The short-landing of baggage, resulting in a passenger being deprived of his personal belongings and clothing throughout an eight-day international pilgrimage tour, undoubtedly constitutes deficiency in service on the part of the carrier," the bench said.However, relying on Article 8.3.4 of the airline's General Conditions of Carriage and the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission's ruling in Shiv Garg v. Lufthansa German Airlines & Ors, it said passengers are advised against packing cash, valuables and essential medicines in checked-in baggage.The commission also noted that Varghese had not produced bills for emergency purchases. It found no evidence to establish his allegation of unfair trade practice.The bench said being without luggage, fresh clothes and basic necessities during an eight-day international journey would naturally cause stress and discomfort. It rejected the airline's USD 40 offer as inadequate."The Opposite Party’s unilateral offer of $40 is wholly disproportionate to the inconvenience suffered by the complainant, a senior citizen passenger over an eight-day international journey," the bench added.It held that the Rs 2 lakh compensation claim was on the higher side, considering the passenger's contributory lapse and the absence of bills proving additional expenses.Final orderAnnounced on November 12, 2026, the order partly allowed the complaint. The commission directed Etihad Airways to pay:Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental agony, physical discomfort and inconvenience.Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.The airline must make the payment within 30 days of receiving the order, failing which the compensation amount, excluding litigation costs, will carry 9% annual interest from the date of the order until realisation.

articles.title: At 15, John Schnatter learned to make pizza while washing dishes; in 1984, he opened a shop in his father’s tavern with $1,600 in used equipment, building a chain that later topped 5,000 restaurants
articles.summary: Discover the incredible journey of John Schnatter, who transformed his dishwashing job into a global pizza empire with over 5,000 restaurants, emphasizing hard work, sacrifice, and passion.
articles.body: A dishwashing job gave John Schnatter something more useful than a pay cheque: a business idea. According to Entrepreneur, Schnatter was 15 years old washing dishes at a pizza restaurant called Rocky’s in Jeffersonville, Indiana. When the kitchen got busy, they pulled him over to make pizza. He paid attention. That habit led to a small shop in 1984 and later a chain of more than 5,000 restaurants.What the dish sink taught him What Rocky’s taught Schnatter was a very simple lesson. The pizza station was right next to the dish sink, so he could see every plate that came back there. The magazine adds that he learned what the customers wanted. A clean plate meant that the pizza was perfect, and a plate with a half-eaten slice meant that it wasn't. There was also a gap he recognised. The national chains offered delivery service, while local businesses that made better quality food did not. That ended up becoming his business idea: make good quality pizza and bring it to the door. It wasn't a difficult idea; it came from what he saw working in a real kitchen.A tavern, a broom closet, and a big sacrifice After graduating from Ball State University, Schnatter returned home. Mick’s Lounge, his father's tavern, was short on money. He sold the Camaro he loved to keep it going. Once the tavern was more stable, he bought $1,600 worth of used restaurant equipment, and then he began making pizza in a broom closet in the back. Papa John's 2007 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows it started in 1984 in his dad's Jeffersonville tavern with $1,600 worth of used equipment. Schnatter recalls selling $5 pizzas from the back and 50-cent beers from the front. He said that his first goal was to make $50,000 a year and have $50,000 in the bank so he could get a date. Years later, he paid $250,000 to buy back the Camaro he had sold. He refers to it as a daily reminder that hard work and sacrifice pay off in the long run.From a single shop to thousands The first proper Papa John's was opened near the tavern. Schnatter said it earned about $9,000 per week in sales, whereas other national franchises earned about $6,000. These were his own numbers. He has mentioned that he believed at age 22 that if he could beat them in one store, he could beat them anywhere. KFC and Long John Silver’s were rapidly expanding through franchising in the region. He chose the same route, saying it was instinctive. USF News reports that the 100th Papa John's was opened in Clarksville, Tennessee, seven years after he started selling pizzas in Mick's Lounge in 1984. As of May 2007, according to the company's filing, Papa John's operated more than 3,000 restaurants in 50 states and 29 countries.What universities saw in his story Later, universities found his story. In 2015, Ball State University announced that Schnatter would deliver the spring commencement address on 2 May and receive an honorary Doctor of Laws degree. Paul W. Ferguson, the university’s president, said Schnatter would inspire the audience with his story of hardwork, perseverance, and willingness to take risks. Ball State’s business college also presented him with an award of achievement in 1993 and a spot in its Hall of Fame in 2004. It said Papa John's had more than 4,600 stores in all 50 states and 34 countries at the time. USF News, reporting on a 2016 talk, adds more. Schnatter had always dreamed of selling pizza and almost quit college to open a franchise of another chain. Papa John's third-quarter 2026 results, released on 5 November 2026, counted 5,969 restaurants in 51 countries and territories as of 27 September 2026. That’s a dramatic turn for a business that began in a broom closet. His advice to young people remains simple: “Find something you love to do and something you’re good at.”You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Who can explain this to him?’: Rijiju tears into Rahul Gandhi over ‘dead economy’ jibe
articles.summary: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Thursday criticised Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his
articles.body: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Thursday criticised Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on India's economy and democracy during a visit to the United States, accusing him of making “highly inaccurate statements about India” on foreign soil.Rijiju said the government would generally prefer not to respond to Rahul's comments but felt compelled to object when he made remarks abroad that, according to the minister, misrepresented the country's economic condition.“We wouldn't want to pay much attention to what Rahul Gandhi says; however, as the Leader of the Opposition, when he goes abroad and makes highly inaccurate statements about India, we feel compelled to register our objection. It is high time he mended his ways,” Rijiju said, according to news agency ANI.Reacting to the Congress leader's assessment of the economy, Rijiju cited the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, saying international institutions recognised India as the fastest-growing major economy.“The entire world acknowledges that India is the fastest-growing economy. It isn't as if we created the IMF or the World Bank; these international financial institutions themselves state that India is currently the fastest-growing major economy. Yet, Rahul Gandhi claims the economy is dead. Who can explain this to him?” he said.Rijiju also accused the Congress leader of damaging the political standing of his party and the opposition through his comments overseas.“I must say that Rahul Gandhi is only succeeding in dragging himself, his party, and the entire opposition further down. No true Indian would want a fellow citizen to go abroad and spout nonsense about their own country,” the minister said.Rijiju questions Rahul's remarks on democracyThe minister also responded to Rahul's allegations of “vote theft” and his criticism of the state of democracy in India. Rijiju argued that Rahul's ability to protest and criticise the government demonstrated the existence of freedom of expression.“He spoke about democracy—alleging 'vote theft' and claiming that democracy does not exist in India. If there were no democracy in India, how would he be able to spend his entire day protesting and hurling insults at PM Modi, the BJP, and the government? If there were no democracy, where would he get the freedom to speak from morning till night?” Rijiju said.“In India, everyone—from an ordinary individual to a political leader—is free to express whatever they wish, all day long. India operates as an incredibly open democracy; yet, despite exercising this freedom, he claims there is no democracy or freedom of speech—what exactly is he trying to prove?” he added.The BJP leader also cited figures he attributed to the IMF on poverty reduction between 2011 and 2023.“The data from the IMF reveals that between 2011 and 2023, more than 500 million (50 crore) people in India have risen above the poverty line. 500 million people have risen out of extreme poverty. In other words, India has set a record for the fastest reduction of poverty in the world,” he said.What Rahul Gandhi said at Columbia UniversityRahul made his remarks during an interaction at Columbia University in New York on Wednesday. Speaking about unemployment and the education system, he said, “The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system.”Responding to moderator Lydia Polgreen's question about young people, Rahul said many, particularly those from middle-class families with formal education, were frustrated because they did not see a clear future for themselves.The remarks have prompted a fresh exchange between the Congress and the BJP over the state of the economy, employment and democratic institutions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2024, Fiji installed a sculptural coral gene bank to preserve resilient corals; within a year, its nursery reported 985 thriving fragments and 95% survival
articles.summary: Discover how Vomo Island Fiji's Sculptural Coral Gene Bank is revolutionizing coral preservation, reporting 985 thriving corals and a remarkable 95% survival rate within just one year.
articles.body: Imagine a steel sculpture under the sea quietly keeping coral alive. That’s what lies underwater in Vomo Island, Fiji. According to Vomo Island Fiji’s announcement, the island launched its coral program back in 2024 with the installation of the Sculptural Coral Gene Bank, a living underwater structure designed to preserve and grow resilient coral species. After one year underwater, the island's Hartz Coral Nursery had 985 healthy fragments with a 95% survival rate. That might feel like good news for anyone who cares and is worried about reefs.From gene bank to nursery The project runs in three phases, and the nursery is the second one. The gene bank, the first phase, holds parent colonies. Coral fragments from the gene bank's parent colonies are raised at the Hartz Coral Nursery. These are then replanted on selected reef sites around the island. The nursery was established with Counting Coral, an organisation dealing with marine conservation. The nursery itself includes six marine-grade stainless steel structures, which were designed by the group. They hold 985 living fragments from various types of coral species that have been chosen because of their resilience and ecological significance. The reefs around Vomo host a wide variety of fish, marine life and coral, which the island views as crucial to the wider marine ecosystem.A strong first year in the water The numbers look encouraging. Survival across six nursery structures ranges from 89% to 99%, with an overall rate of 95%. That's promising, given the challenges of the past year, including changing ocean conditions and seasonal weather events. Vomo calls the milestone the result of years of planning, investment, and environmental stewardship, a foundation for the next phase of reef restoration. This is relevant because a 2020 PLOS ONE review found that restoration projects generally report 60% to 70% survival rates. This, however, is not a direct comparison because the review includes many types of projects, not just nurseries.The people behind the milestone Vomo Island Fiji general manager Leon Pink called the milestone incredibly meaningful. He credited the hard work of the Counting Coral team, island marine biologist Laisenia Rokoua and the Ocean Play team, who continue to care a lot about the project. The reefs are the heart of the Vomo experience. Pink added that to be able to contribute in such a tangible way was very special for the team and the guests. Brooke True, executive director of Counting Coral, called the nursery's success a testament to the Vomo team and the power of sustained reef restoration. She added that every fragment represents future habitat, biodiversity and resilience for the reef. Guests can also learn more about the project through the guided snorkel trips, education programmes, and the continued conservation efforts.What happens next Vomo says outplanting work is set to begin in early 2027. After that, the project is expected to return more than 1,000 coral fragments back to Vomo’s reefs every six to twelve months, creating a continuous cycle of regeneration. Meanwhile, Vomo and Counting Coral will continue to monitor coral health, genetic diversity, and long-term ecosystem outcomes as they expand their restoration work. Monitoring is critical, since, according to the 2020 review, about 60% of such projects reported less than 18 months of monitoring. Care matters a lot too. A 2024 study, ‘Testing the feasibility of coral nurseries in an upwelling area in the North Pacific of Costa Rica,’ showed that survival at a Costa Rican nursery dropped after maintenance was stopped during the COVID-19 lockdown. Restoration, however, cannot be a substitute for action on climate change, the PLOS ONE review adds. For now, these 985 young fragments growing in Fiji’s waters remain a hopeful start.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump meets Putin and Xi as trilateral US, Russia, China talks begin
articles.summary: US president calls both Putin and Xi a ‘friend’ in separate meetings at APEC, ahead of rare three-way talks.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump is meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts for highly anticipated trilateral talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC ) summit.

Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for a “family photo” before beginning talks on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in an unprecedented gathering of the world’s three superpowers.

Opening the meeting, Xi said that it “has groundbreaking significance”.

“The world is at peace when great powers live in harmony,” Xi said, adding that the three countries “should work together to address global challenges”.

In a major statement, the Chinese leader also said “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world,” reported China’s Xinhua news agency.

In Trump’s opening remarks, the US president said the three countries are “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons.

“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” he said. “No peace ever forged by declining opportunities.”

Meanwhile, in his opening remarks, Putin made it clear that the war in Ukraine would be the focus of his conversation, before the three retreated into closed-door talks.

The talks between the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers are unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But the meeting has unnerved smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded.

Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.

The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.

“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader. He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.

Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.

Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.

Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third one-on-one meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.

“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.

Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship. He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.

Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.

“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they’ll come out of this,” Trump told Putin.

A video published by the White House showed the two leaders shaking hands and Trump briefly whispering to Putin at the start of their meeting.

In another video posted by the White House Rapid Response X account, Trump was shown pointing at Putin and saying, “He’s my friend.”

Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said the two leaders “discussed the conflict in Ukraine and bilateral relations issues”.

“The meeting between the Russian and US leaders went well,” Ushakov said, according to Russia’s state news agency TASS, adding that Putin left the talks “in an excellent” mood.

Thursday also features the main event of the APEC summit, as representatives of the 21 Pacific Rim economies gather for discussions that will include high-stakes diplomacy, Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu said, reporting from Shenzhen.

“Xi Jinping, who spoke at the banquet last night during the opening ceremony, said the discussion will centre on promoting mutual openness, innovation-driven growth and results-oriented cooperation,” said Yu.

On the US-China-Russia talks, James Bays, Al Jazeera’s diplomatic editor, said that when it comes to Trump, “his personal role always matters to him”.

But, he added, “something worth bearing in mind: you have three leaders here, Trump, Xi, and Putin. Putin has been in power; he’s been in the main driving seat in Moscow for 26 years; Xi’s been there for 14 years; and they know President Trump only has 26 more months.”

Speaking to Fox News earlier on Thursday, Trump highlighted the pomp surrounding his arrival. Xi greeted Air Force One on the airport tarmac on Wednesday, which contrasted with the more muted greetings offered to other leaders.

“This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody,” Trump said when asked what he wanted to get out of the trilateral summit.

Trump has insisted that nuclear arms control be a central topic of the meeting, despite Beijing’s repeated objections to talks on the issue with Washington and Moscow, which have far larger nuclear arsenals.

articles.title: Rainfall supercharged by El Niño floods roads in south Florida
articles.summary: A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains in South Florida, flooding some streets and homes, closing sections of highways and collapsing the roof of a synagogue on Wednesday.
articles.body: PLANTATION, Fla. — A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains in South Florida, flooding some streets and homes, closing sections of highways and collapsing the roof of a synagogue on Wednesday. On the West Coast, heavy rain and high winds temporarily grounded planes at San Francisco’s airport, disrupted ferry service and flooded roads in Napa County and other wine country areas north of the city. Preliminary figures for Florida showed 15.3 inches (39 centimeters) of rain fell in a 24-hour period ending Wednesday in parts of Broward County, the National Weather Service said. The threat was expected to last through Friday along Florida’s Atlantic Coast with additional rainfall amounts of 12 inches (30 centimeters) possible, the weather service said. A low-pressure system is expected to form near the northern Bahamas. It could become a subtropical or tropical storm over parts of the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts into early next week, according to the National Hurricane Center in Miami. The natural warming cycle called El Niño has disrupted Florida’s typical dry season that runs from October to May, said Alejandra Garcia, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in Miami. El Niño is “helping bring these low pressure systems down toward the southeastern United States, which in turn is causing these heavy precipitation events,” she said. Florida mayor calls the deluge ‘historically significant’ In Florida, Broward County and the cities of Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood declared states of emergency. Hollywood Mayor Josh Levy urged people to avoid driving and unnecessary travel. Portions of the Florida Turnpike and Interstate 95 in Hollywood were closed due to high water and stalled vehicles. The city said it received more than 300 calls for service overnight. “It’s a historically significant rainfall event in the city,” Levy said. Some residents complained that drivers caused a wake that pushed floodwaters into their homes, he said. Heavy rains caused the roof of Temple Sinai in Hollywood to collapse and damaged the roof and flooded hallways at a hospital. No injuries were reported. Rudy Taillard flew back from Texas on Tuesday night to find his apartment complex in the city flooded. “It was insane. The water kept going up,” Taillard said. “If you were living on the first floor, like, you were cooked. It was pretty brutal. Thank God I’m on the top floor.” The highest rainfall amount was recorded in Plantation, where resident Jade Jaime said the storm just kept going all day “and then by the time we went to sleep at night, still just pouring down like it was never going to end.” In Fort Lauderdale, the 5.72 inches (14.5 centimeters) of rain that fell in a downpour ending early Wednesday broke the daily record of 1.8 inches (4.5 centimeters) set in 1959, Garcia said. Officials announced that schools will be closed Thursday in Broward and Miami-Dade counties. In northern Florida, a warning was issued for minor flooding along the St. Johns River. California is loaded with weather concerns The Los Angeles County Fire Department issued an evacuation warning through Friday morning for the Palisades, Hurst and Sunset burn scar areas, warning of a risk of debris flows as a storm approaches. South of San Francisco, a 47-mile (76-kilometer) segment of Highway 1 near Big Sur was closed Wednesday for the same reason. In San Francisco, which set a daily record with 2.28 inches (5.8 centimeters) of rain, the fire department responded to more than 300 calls Wednesday morning, many of which were related to flooding, along with downed trees and electrical wires, Chief Dean Crispen said during a news conference. By Wednesday night, some San Francisco flights were delayed hours because of wind. Areas along the Embarcadero were flooded as waves crashed over barricades recently installed to prevent flooding near the Ferry Building, a waterfront landmark. Officials canceled several ferries leading from the city due to the storm. Several highways were blocked by flooding or debris in Napa, Marin, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties, according to the California Department of Transportation and the California Highway Patrol. Northeast of San Francisco, flooding forced the evacuation of a school in Antioch, according to police and fire officials. Gusts up to 50 mph (80 kph) were forecast for the East Bay region and up to 70 mph (113 kph) for the Altamont Pass, which connects Bay Area highways to I-5 in the Central Valley. Snow accumulations of up to 4 feet (1.2 meters) were forecast through Friday in the highest portions of the Sierra Nevada. Travel issues loom ahead of Thanksgiving week The weather service issued a long-range forecast showing heavy rain is possible along the Atlantic seaboard in Georgia and South Carolina on Saturday, from North Carolina to New York’s Long Island on Sunday and into New England on Sunday and Monday.

articles.title: UK to provide Ukraine with long-range drones as part of £260m package
articles.summary: The prime minister is set to make the announcement at a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin.
articles.body:
The UK will provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones to target Russia beyond the front line, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to announce later.

The drone support will be announced at a meeting in Berlin of Ukraine's allies, the Coalition of the Willing, and is part of a new £260m package to boost its war defences this winter.

The government said the drones are able to fly up to 625 miles (1,000km) and carry heavier warheads, enabling Ukraine to target military production facilities.

The move is the latest sign of a growing British involvement in drone technology for Ukraine. The government said 80% of the package will be spent in the UK.

The Berlin talks come as US President Donald Trump is meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping.

Ahead of that meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in China, Trump said both he and Xi want to see an end to the Ukraine war.

Trump says summit with Xi and Putin in China is 'making history'

Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war

Crimean Bridge attacked again, Russia says

In a statement released ahead of the latest meeting of the group of 36 countries committed to supporting Ukraine in the event of a ceasefire or peace agreement - the government said the UK is also building maritime, logistical and surveillance drones to help Ukraine's war effort.

Burnham, who is co-chairing the meeting, said the UK must do everything it can to make sure Ukraine can defend itself from Russian attacks throughout the winter.

The prime minister said: "Plunging millions of Ukrainians into the freezing cold and starving them of heat and warmth won't see Putin win this war, it will only cement our resolve to support Ukraine.

"That is why I am determined the UK will do everything we can to ensure Ukraine is able to defend itself from Russia's barrage of attacks and systematic striking of critical national infrastructure."

Before this latest support package was announced, government figures put the amount of support provided by the UK for Ukraine since Russia invaded the country in February 2022 at £35.5bn.

In recent days, Ukraine has struck oil refineries in southern Russia, and has repeatedly hit the Crimean Bridge - a significant logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.

Meanwhile, Russian forces have been focused on knocking out power in Ukraine before winter with attacks on critical infrastructure.

The UK is among a number of countries also supplying Ukraine with lightweight missiles which are being used to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

Ukraine's strike rate is now close to 70%, more than double what it was just a couple of months ago, Downing Street said.

The UK also pledged further air defence support this week and sanctioned Russia's 10 major oil producers.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the government was delivering on a promise for more support for Ukraine at the Budget.

"Ukraine's frontline is the frontline for freedom and democracy, and we will stand with them for as long as it takes," he said.

Meanwhile, on Friday Burnham will head to Brussels for a UK-EU summit, where both sides hope to unveil new agreements on food, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

articles.title: Satya Nadella 'admits' Microsoft should have caught Outlook bug before global outage
articles.summary: Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya
articles.body: Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya Nadella has said. In an interview with CNBC’s Jim Cramer, Nadella said that the flaw surfaced only under a particular pattern of traffic. “Of course, we should have done the testing before,” he said.The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella said Microsoft should have designed its systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally.Satya Nadella points to older hardware issueHe also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure. AI tools can help engineers identify software flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed. More frequent updates, he said, can make existing systems less stable. His comments pointed to a trade-off for software providers as they accelerate the release of patches while keeping widely used services online. "Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable," Nadella said. "I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet."The interview came a day after Microsoft used its Ignite conference to pitch Copilot as the main interface for work across its business software. A September overhaul brought its AI tools into one app and introduced usage-based charges for more advanced features. Microsoft typically sells workplace software through licences tied to individual employees. Charging for AI usage gives it another source of revenue if customers buy fewer licences. Nadella said usage already accounts for a substantial part of its Dynamics business, which sells software for functions such as sales and enterprise planning.Nadella said Copilot can also direct requests to models from Anthropic, OpenAI or Microsoft itself. The approach gives Microsoft more flexibility over which models it uses in its own products as its relationship with OpenAI evolves.Asked about local opposition to data centre construction, Nadella said that companies had to show residents what they stood to gain. He pointed to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data centre for about two decades, and said tax revenue had helped pay for a school and other public facilities.Nadella also addressed Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, a major supplier of chips for Microsoft’s Azure cloud. He called Huang a “singular founder” and said that Microsoft remained keen to work with Nvidia’s leadership, including interim chief executive Colette Kress, a former Microsoft employee. He said Nvidia’s board would decide what came next.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.
